h1: What SEO companies charge, and where every rupee goes
metaTitle: What Do SEO Companies Charge? Fees Broken Down
metaDescription: We open one ₹75,000 SEO retainer line by line — salaries, tools, links, content, margin and the 18% GST — so you can see what your fee actually pays for.
answer: Indian SEO companies charge ₹15,000 to ₹5,00,000 a month, but the number that explains the price is the salary bill. A ₹75,000 retainer funds roughly 45 delivered hours, ₹8,000 of shared tooling and about 11% margin. Add 18% GST on top — ₹75,000 invoices at ₹88,500.
takeaways: Salaries set the floor. Indian SEO CTCs run **₹4,00,000 to ₹22,00,000**, which is a loaded cost of roughly ₹330 to ₹1,830 an hour.
A serious tool stack costs an agency ₹50,000–₹80,000 a month. Spread thin across 40 clients it's invisible; spread across a small roster it's a real line item.
Agency margin on a well-run Indian retainer is **10–20%**. Anyone claiming 40% is either overcharging or under-delivering, and you can usually tell which.
₹10,000 a month buys about seven hours of supervised work. That is not an SEO programme — it's a subscription to a PDF.

body: Most agencies won't show you this. Not because it's shameful — because once you can see the line items you can argue with them, and arguing with a range is much harder.
So here is a real ₹75,000/month SEO retainer as a P&L. Ex-GST. Roughly what a mid-size Indian site gets, and roughly how we'd staff one.

callout.title: The link line is the honest one
callout.body: ₹8,500 a month of outreach does not buy four links. It buys about eight hours of a person emailing editors and being ignored, which averages out to roughly one earned placement every one to two months. Any agency promising ten links for that money is buying them.

sections.h2: Salaries set the floor, and nothing moves them
body: An agency's price cannot go below its payroll for long. So the salary market is the real ceiling on how cheap SEO can honestly get in India.

These are the bands the Indian market broadly runs on. They vary by city — Bengaluru and Gurgaon sit at the top, tier-2 cities can be 25–35% lower — and by whether the employer is an agency or a product company, which is usually a 20–40% gap in the product company's favour.

bullets: **Loaded cost is CTC × ~1.3, divided by ~130 billable hours a month.** The 1.3 is PF, gratuity, a laptop, a seat, health cover and training. The 130 is what's left of 176 working hours after internal meetings, sick days, leave and the hours nobody can bill to anyone.
**This is why a ₹15,000 retainer only ever gets a fresher.** It's the only band the arithmetic permits, and freshers unsupervised are how sites end up with duplicate title tags across 4,000 URLs.

**And why senior time is rationed.** At ₹1,800 an hour, nine hours of a lead is ₹16,000 — over a fifth of a ₹75,000 retainer for roughly two hours a week. That's the correct amount. It's also why agencies quietly substitute juniors when margins get tight.

sections.h2: The tool stack, and why it isn't optional
body: You can do SEO with Search Console and a spreadsheet. You cannot do competitive SEO with them, because you can't see anything happening outside your own domain.
Approximate list prices at the time of writing, converted at roughly ₹88 to the dollar. Vendors change these regularly, so treat them as an order of magnitude, not a quote:
bullets: **Ahrefs** — entry tier around $129/mo, roughly **₹11,000**. Higher tiers with more seats and credits run 2–3.5x that.
**Semrush** — entry tier around $140/mo, roughly **₹12,000**. Similar multiples upward.
**Screaming Frog** — around £199/year, roughly **₹1,800/mo**. Free below 500 URLs, which is genuinely enough for a small site.
**Rank tracking, log analysis, content tooling, QA and monitoring** — another ₹15,000–₹35,000/mo across a team.
**Total for a working agency stack: ₹50,000–₹80,000 a month**, before any per-client costs.

callout.title: How the tool line hides
callout.body: An agency with 60 clients allocates under ₹1,200 of tooling per client and never mentions it. We take three new clients a month, so the same stack costs about ₹8,000 per account. That's a genuine argument for the big agency's price — and the reason their senior people are stretched across 60 accounts is the argument against it.

body: Two numbers sit on top of the work, and both are routinely left out of the conversation until the invoice arrives.

**Margin.** A well-run Indian services agency nets 10–20%. Below 10% it can't survive a client leaving; above 25% it's usually running juniors on senior rates. On our ₹75,000 example, ₹8,000 is about 11%. We'd rather show you that than pretend we're a charity — an agency with no margin is an agency that will quietly cut your hours to survive the quarter.

**GST.** Almost every Indian agency quotes ex-GST and then adds **18%**. That ₹75,000 retainer invoices at **₹88,500**. Over a year that's ₹1,62,000 of tax on ₹9,00,000 of fees. If your business is GST-registered you claim it as input credit, so it's a cash-flow cost rather than a real one. If you're not registered, it's a straight 18% price rise you didn't budget for.
The phrase to watch for on a quote is "plus taxes as applicable". It's accurate, it's legal, and it means your ₹40,000 budget is really a ₹33,900 budget.
Run the same sum backwards on the packages advertised across Indian marketplaces.

Of ₹10,000, tools and overhead still take their cut — a smaller stack, but not zero. Call it ₹7,000 reaching delivery. At a mid-level ₹1,000 blended cost, that's **seven hours a month**. Under two hours a week, including the time spent producing the report that proves the two hours happened.

Staff it entirely with a fresher at ₹350 an hour and you get twenty hours instead. Which sounds better until you consider that twenty unsupervised hours is enough time to deploy a sitewide canonical error, and not nearly enough to notice one.

This isn't an argument that cheap agencies are dishonest. Most aren't. It's that the arithmetic can't be beaten, and the pitch deck is written as though it can. [The lowest price of SEO](/cost/lowest-price-of-seo) takes the ₹2,999 packages apart the same way.

callout.title: The seven-hour test
callout.body: Before you sign anything under ₹25,000/mo, ask what could be finished in seven to twenty hours. If the honest answer is "a report and some meta descriptions", buy that knowingly — it's occasionally the right purchase for a five-page site. Just don't expect it to move a lead count.

sections.h2: How to read what a quote leaves out
body: A quote's silences are more informative than its inclusions. These four are the ones worth chasing.
Then compare like with like. Two proposals for "SEO — ₹60,000/mo" can differ by a factor of three in actual work, and neither is lying.
numbered: **No hours or headcount anywhere.** Not necessarily bad — some agencies genuinely price by output. But then the output must be specified: how many pages, how many fixes, how many placements.

**Content counted in articles, not in researched articles.** A 700-word AI-assembled post and a 1,500-word piece with a subject-matter interview both count as "1 blog". One of them ranks. See [content writing cost in India](/cost/content-writing-cost-india).

**Links quoted per placement.** Per-placement pricing means [bought placements](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies), because earned ones can't be guaranteed to a schedule. We bill link work by hours for exactly this reason.
**No line for reporting or analysis.** If nobody's paid to interpret the data, you'll receive a dashboard export and a cheerful summary, which is how twelve months disappear.
**"Plus taxes as applicable."** Add 18% before you compare it to anything.

faqs.q: What do SEO companies charge per month in India?
faqs.a: Quotes cluster between ₹15,000 and ₹5,00,000 a month. The working middle is ₹40,000 for a small local site and ₹75,000–₹1,50,000 for a competitive national keyword set. All of it is normally quoted ex-GST, so add 18% before comparing to your budget.

faqs.q: How much of my SEO fee actually goes on my site?
faqs.a: On a well-run retainer, roughly 70–75% reaches delivery. The rest is tools, overhead and margin. On our ₹75,000 example that's about ₹54,000 of people-time, which works out to around 45 hours plus four content pieces.

faqs.q: How much do SEO agencies pay their staff in India?
faqs.a: Executives typically ₹4–6 lakh CTC, specialists ₹7–10 lakh, senior and technical SEOs ₹10–16 lakh, and leads ₹16–22 lakh or more. Metro salaries run highest; tier-2 cities sit 25–35% lower. Loaded onto billable hours, that's roughly ₹330 to ₹1,830 an hour.

faqs.q: Do SEO agency fees include GST?
faqs.a: Rarely. Indian agencies almost always quote ex-GST and add 18% on the invoice, so ₹75,000 bills at ₹88,500. GST-registered businesses recover it as input credit, making it a cash-flow item. If you're not registered, treat it as a real 18% increase.

faqs.q: Why is one agency ₹30,000 and another ₹1,20,000 for the same website?
faqs.a: Usually seniority and volume. The ₹30,000 quote is one generalist part-time; the ₹1,20,000 quote is four specialists with a funded link budget. Ask both for hours by role. The answer either arrives in ten seconds or it doesn't arrive at all, and that itself is the comparison.

faqs.q: Is a higher SEO retainer always better?
faqs.a: No. Past roughly ₹1,50,000 a month, coordination starts absorbing the increase — more people means more handoffs. Buy the band that matches your site's complexity, not the one that sounds serious. A 25-page services site cannot usefully spend ₹3,00,000 a month.
